easy.question: Who heard about all that the Lord had done for Moses and Israel?
answers: Jethro
Pharaoh
Aaron
easy.explanation: The first verse says that Jethro heard about Israel’s exodus from Egypt and the Lord’s deeds.

easy.question: Who was Zipporah?
answers: Jethro’s daughter
Moses’ wife
Moses’ sister
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly calls Zipporah “Moses’ wife.”

easy.question: What were the names of Moses’ two sons?
answers: Aaron and Gershom
Eliezer and Joshua
Gershom and Eliezer
easy.explanation: The verses name the two sons as Gershom and Eliezer.

medium.question: Why was Moses’ son named Gershom?
answers: Because Moses had been an alien in a strange land
Because he was born in Egypt
Because the Lord saved him from Pharaoh
medium.explanation: Moses said, “I have been an alien in a strange land,” so he named his son Gershom.

medium.question: What connection did the names of Moses’ two sons have to his life?
answers: Both were named after places in Egypt
One recalled that he was an alien, and the other recalled his deliverance
Both were named after Jethro’s sons
medium.explanation: Gershom recalled Moses’ being an alien, while Eliezer recalled God’s help and deliverance from Pharaoh’s sword.

medium.question: In the phrase “after he had sent her back,” what does the phrase explain?
answers: That Zipporah had given birth to her sons
That Zipporah had arrived in Midian
That Moses had sent Zipporah away or separated from her
medium.explanation: The verse says that Jethro took Zipporah after Moses had sent her back.

challenge.question: What does the mention of the sons’ names show about their importance?
answers: The names preserved important memories from Moses’ life
The names were chosen only because they were short
The names came from Egyptian kings
challenge.explanation: Each name is connected to an important event: Gershom to Moses’ exile and Eliezer to God’s help and deliverance.

challenge.question: From what did God deliver Moses, according to the verse?
answers: From exile in Midian
From Pharaoh’s sword
From a lack of food
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “he delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh,” which explains the name Eliezer.

challenge.question: What idea sequence appears in the verses concerning Moses’ family?
answers: Eliezer is mentioned first, then Gershom, and finally Zipporah
Jethro heard first, Pharaoh saved Moses, and then the sons were born
Zipporah is mentioned first, then Gershom, and finally Eliezer
challenge.explanation: The verses move from mentioning Zipporah to Gershom and finally to Eliezer.

answers: From exile in Midian

questions.explanation: The verse says, “he delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh,” which explains the name Eliezer.

paragraphs.title: Moses’ Family Comes to the Wilderness

easy.question: Who came to Moses in the wilderness?
answers: Jethro, his sons, and his wife
Pharaoh and his servants
Aaron and the Israelites
easy.explanation: The verse says that Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, came with his sons and wife.

easy.question: Where was Moses camped when Jethro came to him?
answers: In the king’s palace
In the wilderness, at the mount of God
In the city of Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses was camped in the wilderness at the mount of God.

easy.question: How did Moses welcome his father-in-law?
answers: He stayed in his tent
He sent a messenger to him
He went out to meet him, bowed, and kissed him
easy.explanation: Moses went out to meet Jethro, bowed to him, and kissed him.

medium.question: Why did Moses go out to meet his father-in-law?
answers: Because Jethro had come to him
Because Jethro had sent him to Egypt
Because Moses was looking for the Israelites
medium.explanation: Jethro came to Moses, so Moses went out to meet and welcome him.

medium.question: In the phrase “Moses went out to meet his father-in-law,” what does “to meet” show?
answers: That Moses went far away from him
That Moses went to see and welcome him
That Moses went after he had left
medium.explanation: Moses went toward Jethro in order to meet and welcome him.

medium.question: Who is meant by “her two sons with her”?
answers: Pharaoh’s daughter
Jethro’s daughter
Moses’ wife
medium.explanation: Jethro said that Moses’ wife had come with him, and that her two sons were with her.

challenge.question: What is the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: Jethro came, identified himself to Moses, and Moses welcomed him
Moses blessed Jethro, Jethro came, and then identified himself
Jethro entered the tent, Moses searched for him, and then Jethro came
challenge.explanation: First Jethro came, then he told Moses that he was his father-in-law, and finally Moses went out to welcome him.

challenge.question: What does “they asked each other of their welfare” show?
answers: Only Jethro asked about Moses
Moses and Jethro greeted and asked about each other
They parted without speaking
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the greeting and concern were mutual between Moses and Jethro.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the fact that Moses went out, bowed, and kissed Jethro?
answers: Moses was afraid of Jethro
Moses did not know Jethro
Moses treated him with respect and affection
challenge.explanation: Going out to meet someone, bowing, and kissing express an honorable and affectionate welcome.

answers: Jethro came, identified himself to Moses, and Moses welcomed him

questions.explanation: First Jethro came, then he told Moses that he was his father-in-law, and finally Moses went out to welcome him.

answers: Only Jethro asked about Moses

They parted without speaking
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that the greeting and concern were mutual between Moses and Jethro.

questions.question: What can be understood from the fact that Moses went out, bowed, and kissed Jethro?
answers: Moses was afraid of Jethro
Moses did not know Jethro
Moses treated him with respect and affection
questions.explanation: Going out to meet someone, bowing, and kissing express an honorable and affectionate welcome.

paragraphs.title: Moses Tells the Story and Jethro Blesses God

easy.question: To whom did Moses tell all that the Lord had done?
answers: His father-in-law, Jethro
Aaron
The elders of Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says that Moses told his father-in-law Jethro about the Lord’s deeds.

easy.question: How did Jethro react when he heard about the goodness the Lord had done for Israel?
answers: He became angry
He rejoiced
He became afraid
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says that Jethro rejoiced over the goodness the Lord had done for Israel.

easy.question: What did Jethro offer to God?
answers: Clothing and gifts
Bread and water
A burnt offering and sacrifices
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says that Jethro brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God.

medium.question: Why did Jethro bless the Lord?
answers: Because the Lord delivered Israel from Egypt and Pharaoh
Because Moses became a leader
Because Israel reached the wilderness
medium.explanation: Jethro blessed the Lord for delivering the people from Egypt and Pharaoh.

medium.question: In the phrase “all the travail that had come upon them by the way,” what does “travail” mean?
answers: Joy
Troubles and hardships
Gifts
medium.explanation: “Travail” means troubles and hardships; the verse refers to what Israel experienced on the journey.

medium.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: Jethro offered sacrifices, Moses told the story, and then Israel was delivered
Israel ate, Jethro blessed God, and then Moses told the story
Moses told the story, Jethro rejoiced and blessed God, and then they offered sacrifices and ate
medium.explanation: First Moses told Jethro what had happened, then Jethro rejoiced and blessed the Lord, and finally he offered sacrifices and they ate together.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them”?
answers: The Lord overcame the Egyptians’ plot against Israel
The Egyptians helped Israel in the wilderness
Israel planned to harm the Egyptians
challenge.explanation: Jethro understood that the Lord’s greatness was shown by overcoming the Egyptians’ proud plan to harm Israel.

challenge.question: What does Jethro emphasize when he mentions both the troubles and the deliverance?
answers: The troubles were more important than the deliverance
The Lord’s goodness and deliverance are what should bring joy
Moses did not know what had happened to the people
challenge.explanation: Although Moses described the hardships, Jethro focused on God’s goodness and deliverance and responded with joy and praise.

challenge.question: Who is explicitly said to have eaten bread with Jethro before God?
answers: Pharaoh and all Egypt
Moses and his sons alone
Aaron and all the elders of Israel
challenge.explanation: Verse 12 says that Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them”?
answers: The Lord overcame the Egyptians’ plot against Israel
The Egyptians helped Israel in the wilderness
Israel planned to harm the Egyptians
questions.explanation: Jethro understood that the Lord’s greatness was shown by overcoming the Egyptians’ proud plan to harm Israel.

answers: The troubles were more important than the deliverance

Moses did not know what had happened to the people
questions.explanation: Although Moses described the hardships, Jethro focused on God’s goodness and deliverance and responded with joy and praise.

questions.question: Who is explicitly said to have eaten bread with Jethro before God?
answers: Pharaoh and all Egypt
Moses and his sons alone
Aaron and all the elders of Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says that Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.

easy.question: Who sat to judge the people?
answers: Moses
Jethro
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses sat to judge the people.

easy.question: From when until when did the people stand before Moses?
answers: From noon until night
From morning until evening
From evening until morning
easy.explanation: The verses say that the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.

easy.question: Who asked Moses why he sat alone?
answers: The people
Aaron
Moses’ father-in-law
easy.explanation: Moses’ father-in-law saw what he was doing and asked why he sat alone.

medium.question: Why did the people come to Moses?
answers: To go to war
To inquire of God and bring their matters before him
To eat together
medium.explanation: Moses explained that the people came to inquire of God and to have him decide their cases.

medium.question: What did Moses do when people had a matter or dispute?
answers: He sent them into the wilderness
He ignored them
He judged between them and taught them God’s statutes and laws
medium.explanation: Moses said that he judged between people and made known God’s statutes and laws.

medium.question: In the phrase “all the people stand by thee,” what does “stand by” show?
answers: They stood and waited
They were sleeping
They were fleeing
medium.explanation: The people stood before Moses and waited for him to handle their matters, from morning until evening.

challenge.question: What practical problem could Jethro see from the people standing before Moses all day?
answers: The people did not know Moses
The people had no questions or disputes
The burden on Moses was very great
challenge.explanation: Since the people waited with Moses all day, it was clear that he alone carried a heavy burden of judging and teaching.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “thyself alone” show about how Moses handled the people?
answers: He handled their matters himself, without other judges being mentioned here
He did not want to speak with the people
He was far from Israel’s camp
challenge.explanation: Jethro emphasized that Moses was sitting alone, handling all the people’s matters by himself.

challenge.question: Which sequence correctly describes Moses’ explanation?
answers: The people came to him, he went to war, and then he returned
When someone had a matter, he came to Moses, who judged and taught God’s laws
Moses taught the people, then they brought him gifts, and finally he judged
challenge.explanation: Moses explained that when a person had a matter, he came to him, and Moses judged between the parties and taught God’s laws.

questions.question: What practical problem could Jethro see from the people standing before Moses all day?
answers: The people did not know Moses
The people had no questions or disputes
The burden on Moses was very great
questions.explanation: Since the people waited with Moses all day, it was clear that he alone carried a heavy burden of judging and teaching.

questions.question: What does the phrase “thyself alone” show about how Moses handled the people?
answers: He handled their matters himself, without other judges being mentioned here
He did not want to speak with the people
He was far from Israel’s camp
questions.explanation: Jethro emphasized that Moses was sitting alone, handling all the people’s matters by himself.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes Moses’ explanation?
answers: The people came to him, he went to war, and then he returned
When someone had a matter, he came to Moses, who judged and taught God’s laws
Moses taught the people, then they brought him gifts, and finally he judged
questions.explanation: Moses explained that when a person had a matter, he came to him, and Moses judged between the parties and taught God’s laws.

paragraphs.title: Jethro Warns of the Burden and Gives Advice

easy.question: Who said to Moses, “The thing that thou doest is not good”?
answers: Moses’ father-in-law
The people
Aaron
easy.explanation: Moses’ father-in-law told him that the way he was working was not good.

easy.question: Upon whom would the burden be too heavy?
answers: Moses alone
Moses and the people
Moses’ father-in-law alone
easy.explanation: Jethro said, “both thou, and this people,” meaning that the burden would affect both Moses and the people.

easy.question: What did Moses need to teach the people?
answers: How to leave Egypt
How to build the tabernacle
The ordinances, the way they should walk, and the work they should do
easy.explanation: Moses was to teach them God’s ordinances and laws, the way they should walk, and the work they should do.

medium.question: Why could Moses not do everything by himself?
answers: Because the task was too heavy for him
Because the people did not want to listen
Because he did not know the way
medium.explanation: Jethro explained that the task was too heavy for Moses and that he could not carry it alone.

medium.question: What did Moses’ father-in-law advise him to do after warning him?
answers: Leave the people
Listen to him and accept his advice
Stop speaking with God
medium.explanation: Jethro said, “Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel,” and urged Moses to follow his advice.

medium.question: In the phrase “Thou wilt surely wear away,” what does it mean?
answers: You will rejoice greatly
You will hurry away
You will become exhausted and collapse
medium.explanation: In context, the words warn that Moses would become weak and collapse under the burden.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repeated words “both thou, and this people”?
answers: The burden on Moses would also harm the people
Only the people were responsible for the problem
Moses and the people needed to leave
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the system burdened not only Moses but also the people who needed his help.

challenge.question: What is the significance of “God shall be with thee” in Jethro’s advice?
answers: Moses no longer needed to speak with the people
The plan should be carried out while relying on God
Moses’ father-in-law would replace God
challenge.explanation: Jethro suggested a practical change while emphasizing that Moses should continue to act with God’s help.

challenge.question: Which best describes Moses’ role according to these verses?
answers: To judge every person in the nation alone
To tell the people only what work they should do
To bring the people’s causes before God and teach them His laws and ways
challenge.explanation: The verses describe both parts of Moses’ role: bringing matters before God and guiding the people in His laws, ways, and commands.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the repeated words “both thou, and this people”?
answers: The burden on Moses would also harm the people
Only the people were responsible for the problem
Moses and the people needed to leave
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the system burdened not only Moses but also the people who needed his help.

answers: Moses no longer needed to speak with the people

questions.explanation: Jethro suggested a practical change while emphasizing that Moses should continue to act with God’s help.

questions.question: Which best describes Moses’ role according to these verses?
answers: To judge every person in the nation alone
To tell the people only what work they should do
To bring the people’s causes before God and teach them His laws and ways
questions.explanation: The verses describe both parts of Moses’ role: bringing matters before God and guiding the people in His laws, ways, and commands.

easy.question: Who would judge the people according to Jethro’s advice?
answers: Rulers and leaders
The people alone
Moses alone
easy.explanation: Moses was to appoint rulers who would take responsibility for judging the people.

easy.question: What would the judges do with small matters?
answers: Bring them to Moses
Judge them themselves
Ignore them
easy.explanation: The verse says that the judges would judge every small matter themselves.

easy.question: Which quality was required of the men who were chosen?
answers: That they be wealthy
That they be young
That they fear God
easy.explanation: The required qualities included fearing God.

medium.question: Why were rulers appointed to judge the people?
answers: To lighten the burden on Moses
To abolish judgment
To keep the people away from Moses
medium.explanation: The rulers would share the burden with Moses and make the work easier for him.

medium.question: How would disputes be handled according to these verses?
answers: All disputes would be brought to Moses
Small matters would be brought to Moses first
The rulers would judge small matters, and great matters would be brought to Moses
medium.explanation: The rulers would handle small matters, while great matters would be brought to Moses.

medium.question: In the phrase “men of truth, hating covetousness,” what does “covetousness” mean?
answers: Dishonest profit or bribery
Physical strength
Sadness and worry
medium.explanation: The phrase describes people who reject corrupt gain and bribery.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “let them judge the people at all seasons”?
answers: Judgment would take place only on holidays
The rulers would be available to judge regularly
Judgment would take place only when Moses was present
challenge.explanation: The phrase means that the rulers would handle cases continually, not only on special occasions.

challenge.question: What does the condition “If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so” teach?
answers: The plan also depended on God’s approval and command
Moses did not need to choose the judges
The people could cancel the plan
challenge.explanation: Jethro emphasized that the plan depended not only on human decision but also on God’s approval.

challenge.question: What was the meaning of dividing the rulers into rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens?
answers: All rulers would oversee the same group
Only rulers of thousands would judge
A graded system of responsibility and judgment was created
challenge.explanation: The different levels created an organized system in which leaders handled different groups and levels of cases.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “let them judge the people at all seasons”?
answers: Judgment would take place only on holidays
The rulers would be available to judge regularly
Judgment would take place only when Moses was present
questions.explanation: The phrase means that the rulers would handle cases continually, not only on special occasions.

questions.question: What does the condition “If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so” teach?
answers: The plan also depended on God’s approval and command
Moses did not need to choose the judges
The people could cancel the plan
questions.explanation: Jethro emphasized that the plan depended not only on human decision but also on God’s approval.

answers: All rulers would oversee the same group
Only rulers of thousands would judge
A graded system of responsibility and judgment was created
questions.explanation: The different levels created an organized system in which leaders handled different groups and levels of cases.

paragraphs.title: Moses Puts the Advice into Practice

easy.question: Whose advice did Moses follow?
answers: His father-in-law’s
The people’s
The rulers’
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Moses hearkened to the voice of his father in law.”

easy.question: Who chose the able men?
answers: Jethro
Moses
The people
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Moses chose able men out of all Israel.”

easy.question: Where did Moses’ father-in-law go at the end of the passage?
answers: To Israel’s camp
To Mount Sinai
To his own land
easy.explanation: The passage ends by saying that he went into his own land.

medium.question: Why did Moses appoint rulers over the people?
answers: To divide the judicial work and make it easier for him
To keep the people away from him
To replace Aaron
medium.explanation: The rulers judged most cases, while only the difficult matters were brought to Moses.

medium.question: In the phrase “Moses chose able men out of all Israel,” what does “able men” mean?
answers: Young men only
Qualified and capable men
Men who had served in the army
medium.explanation: They were chosen to lead and judge, so they were qualified, trustworthy, and capable men.

medium.question: What happened after Moses chose the able men?
answers: His father-in-law immediately returned home
The people stopped bringing cases to him
Moses made them heads over the people
medium.explanation: After choosing them, Moses made them heads over the people.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens?
answers: Leadership was divided into several levels and groups
Each ruler judged the entire nation alone
Only rulers of thousands were allowed to judge
challenge.explanation: The different levels and groups show an organized and graded leadership system.

challenge.question: What change resulted from the system described in these verses?
answers: All problems were immediately transferred to Moses
Most cases were handled by the rulers, while Moses handled only difficult ones
The rulers dealt only with military matters
challenge.explanation: The verses say that the rulers judged small matters, while difficult matters were brought to Moses.

challenge.question: Who is meant by “he went his way into his own land”?
answers: Moses
The people of Israel
Moses’ father-in-law
challenge.explanation: The subject at the beginning of the verse is Moses’ father-in-law, whom Moses allowed to depart.

questions.question: What can be learned from the rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens?
answers: Leadership was divided into several levels and groups
Each ruler judged the entire nation alone
Only rulers of thousands were allowed to judge
questions.explanation: The different levels and groups show an organized and graded leadership system.

questions.question: What change resulted from the system described in these verses?
answers: All problems were immediately transferred to Moses
Most cases were handled by the rulers, while Moses handled only difficult ones
The rulers dealt only with military matters
questions.explanation: The verses say that the rulers judged small matters, while difficult matters were brought to Moses.

questions.question: Who is meant by “he went his way into his own land”?
answers: Moses
The people of Israel
Moses’ father-in-law
questions.explanation: The subject at the beginning of the verse is Moses’ father-in-law, whom Moses allowed to depart.
